name: A Song of Ice and Fire: Tabletop Miniatures Game
description: A competitive tabletop miniatures wargame set in the world of George R.R. Martin's novels . Players command armies from rival Houses (such as Stark and Lannister), maneuvering ranks of infantry, cavalry, and legendary heroes across the battlefield. The game uses rank-and-file movement trays and alternating activations, emphasizing strategic use of characters and tactics in recreating the epic conflicts of Westeros.

name: Adeptus Titanicus
description: A tabletop miniatures game of epic Titan battles set in the Warhammer 40,000 universe's Horus Heresy era. Players control giant Imperial Titans and war machines, managing plasma reactors and void shields in tactical engagements. The game uses detailed rules for movement, damage, and orders, focusing on the strategic positioning and combat of towering god- machines on the battlefield.

name: Aeronautica Imperialis
description: A fast-paced aerial combat miniatures game set in the Warhammer 40,000 universe. Players command squadrons of aircraft – from Imperial Navy fighters to Ork jets – in dogfights and bombing runs across the skies. Movement and combat use maneuver templates and dice rolls to simulate altitude and speed, emphasizing tactical maneuvering and timing as players vie for air superiority.

name: Age of Fantasy
description: A one-page fantasy miniatures wargame set in a dark magical world . It features streamlined rules for large-scale battles between classic fantasy armies (humans, elves, orcs, undead and more), allowing players to field units of warriors and monsters with simple, fast-paced mechanics. Designed for flexibility, it lets players use any models to reenact epic clashes of swords and sorcery while keeping gameplay quick and accessible.

name: BattleTech
description: A classic science-fiction miniature wargame featuring futuristic mech combat. Players command one or more BattleMechs – giant humanoid war machines – on a hex-gridded battlefield, managing movement, weapon fire, and heat in turn-based engagements . The game emphasizes detailed damage tracking and tactical decision-making, as armored mechs duel with lasers, missiles, and autocannons in a war-torn future.

name: Black Powder
description: A 28 mm historical miniature wargame set during the Horse & Musket era of the 18th and 19th centuries . The rules cover large battles from conflicts like the Napoleonic Wars, American War of Independence, and Civil War. Players command brigades of infantry, cavalry, and artillery formed in ranks, issuing orders through commanders. The game emphasizes elegant, fast-flowing play and recreating historical tactics of massed black-powder warfare.

name: Black Seas
description: A naval miniatures wargame focusing on the Age of Sail, roughly 1770–1830 . Players command fleets of historical sailing ships (from nimble brigs to mighty ships-of-the-line) and engage in tactical sea battles. Wind direction, broadside volleys, and boarding actions all play a part as players maneuver their vessels across the waves. The game's detailed yet fast-1 2 3 4 5 1 paced rules capture the flavor of naval combat in the golden age of tall ships.

name: Blood & Plunder
description: A 28 mm historical miniatures war game set in the 17th-century Caribbean during the golden age of piracy . Players lead crews of pirates, privateers, or colonial forces in scenarios on land or at sea, using period ships for naval battles and musket-armed troops for island skirmishes. The game features an innovative initiative system (using playing cards) and emphasizes cinematic, fast-paced action with a high level of historical detail in uniforms, ships, and weaponry.

name: Blood Bowl
description: A fantasy football-themed miniatures game set in the Warhammer universe. Players coach teams of brutal fantasy creatures (such as humans, orcs, elves, or undead) competing in violent, gridiron-style matches. The game combines strategy and luck as players move miniatures on a board, throw passes, make tackles, and even cast the occasional spell . While humorous in tone, it features robust rules for league play, allowing teams and star players to develop over a series of matches.

name: Blood Red Skies
description: A World War II aerial combat miniatures game where players command formations of fighter aircraft in battle . The game is fast- paced, using a unique ‘Advantage' system to represent energy and altitude in dogfights. Players maneuver iconic WWII planes (such as Spitfires and Messerschmitts) on the tabletop, attempting to outflank opponents and gain superior positioning. The rules emphasize quick decision-making and cinematic dogfights, with multiple aircraft per side engaging in swirling battles in the sky.

name: Bolt Action
description: A World War II tabletop wargame that emphasizes tactical, squad-level combat . Using 28 mm miniatures, players recreate battles across theaters of WWII, commanding infantry squads supported by tanks, artillery, and aircraft . The game's innovative order dice activation system creates a dynamic and unpredictable turn sequence , requiring careful planning as players alternate pulling dice to activate units. Bolt Action's rules balance historical flavor with accessible gameplay, allowing refights of anything from Normandy firefights to Eastern Front tank engagements.

name: Bushido
description: An oriental fantasy skirmish miniatures game for two players . Set in the mystical Jwar Isles (inspired by feudal Japan and East Asian mythology), each player commands a small warband of 5–15 models, including samurai, monks, oni demons, and other legendary warriors. The game emphasizes close combat, martial arts skills, and Ki powers (magical abilities), with a dice-based combat system that rewards tactical positioning and timing. Tight 2′×2′ battlefields with detailed terrain make for intense battles where every move is critical.

name: Chain of Command
description: A platoon-scale World War II miniatures wargame focusing on realistic tactical actions . Players take command of an infantry platoon (plus support units like tanks or heavy weapons) and must maneuver squads across terrain using real-life tactics – fire and movement, ambushes, and suppression. The rules introduce an elegant command-and-control system (with command dice) that forces players to manage limited orders and react to battlefield chaos. Emphasis is placed on historical accuracy in unit behavior, making for tense engagements that capture the feel of WWII platoon combat.

name: Conquest: The Last Argument of Kings
description: A mass-battle fantasy wargame 6 7 8 9 9 9 10 11 2 from Para Bellum Games that uses a modern take on rank-and-file combat . Players command large armies divided into regiments of infantry, cavalry, and monsters, drawn from unique factions in the world of Ea (such as the Old Dominion or Dweghom). The game features innovative alternating activations (with a command stack mechanic) and scalable rules to handle big battles smoothly. With detailed miniatures and a rich lore, Conquest brings epic fantasy warfare to the tabletop with an emphasis on maneuver warfare and army list customization.

name: Deadzone
description: A sci-fi skirmish miniatures game set in a futuristic quarantine zone . Players lead small teams of elite soldiers or alien raiders in close-quarters battles amid urban warzones called “Deadzones.” The game uses an innovative cube-grid movement system and three-dimensional terrain, creating fast, brutal firefights where cover and positioning are crucial . With alternating activations and dice-based combat resolution, Deadzone delivers quick, tactical gameplay as rival strike teams clash over objectives such as resources, intel, or survival.

name: Dropfleet Commander
description: A tabletop game of orbital space combat set in the 27th century . Players command fleets of lavishly detailed starships – from nimble frigates to massive battleships – engaging in battles for control of planets. The game uniquely focuses on orbital warfare: managing altitude orbits and balancing between space superiority and ground invasion support. Commanders deploy carriers to launch strike craft and issue orders while using a sensor and signature system to simulate detection and stealth. Dropfleet Commander emphasizes strategic planning over a full planetary theater, capturing the challenges of combined space and ground operations.

name: Dropzone Commander
description: A 10 mm scale sci-fi wargame of planetary invasion and urban combat . Players control combined-arms battlegroups in the war-torn 27th century, featuring factions like the UCM, Scourge, PHR, and Shaltari. The game revolves around rapid deployment via dropships: tanks, APCs, mechs, and infantry are ferried into battle, making mobility and timing key factors. Combat occurs in dense city terrain with an emphasis on scenario objectives (like securing intel or critical sites). Dropzone Commander's rules are designed for efficient, massed battles, offering tactical depth through its innovative drop-and-deploy mechanics.

name: Dystopian Wars
description: A tabletop wargame of steampunk naval battles set in an alternate late 19th century . Players command fleets from Victorian-era superpowers (like the British Crown, Prussian Empire, or Empire of the Blazing Sun), featuring retro-futuristic warships, submersibles, and airships powered by exotic technology. The game's mechanics capture naval combat with a twist of sci-fi: squadrons exchange broadsides and unleash tesla weapons or clockwork drones. With rules encompassing sea, air, and land units, Dystopian Wars delivers a grand, cinematic experience of all-out industrial-age warfare with a steampunk flair.

name: Flames of War
description: A World War II tabletop miniatures game that lets players recreate historical battles with company-level forces . Using 15 mm scale models, players field formations of tanks, infantry, artillery, and aircraft drawn from actual WWII units. The rules cover all theaters of the war and emphasize combined-arms tactics: armor, infantry, and support must work 12 13 14 15 16 17 18 3 together to achieve objectives. Flames of War offers both competitive play and historical scenarios, with straightforward mechanics (e.g. unit stat cards and handfuls of dice for shooting) that capture the feel of WWII combat while remaining accessible.

name: Frostgrave
description: A fantasy skirmish wargame in which each player assumes the role of a wizard leading a band of adventurers into a frozen, ruined city . Players assemble small warbands (typically a wizard, their apprentice, and up to eight soldiers) and compete to retrieve magical treasures amid the crumbling remains of Felstad. Spells play a major role – wizards can cast from ten schools of magic, with effects ranging from fireballs to animating the dead. The game is scenario-driven and campaign-focused: warbands gain experience and loot over multiple games, developing their wizard's powers in an ongoing narrative of exploration and battles against rival sorcerers.

name: Gaslands
description: A tabletop game of post-apocalyptic vehicular mayhem . With fast and cinematic rules, it is designed to be played with toy cars as miniatures, allowing players to ram, skid, and race through the wreckage of a burnt-out Earth . Players customize and arm their vehicles (like cars, buggies, or war rigs) with weapons from machine guns to rocket boosters. The game uses movement templates and skid dice to handle high-octane stunts and crashes. Whether racing for the finish line or battling in an arena of death, Gaslands delivers high-speed, destructive action in the spirit of Mad Max.

name: Grimdark Future
description: A one-page futuristic wargame set in a war-torn sci-fi galaxy . The game features streamlined rules that allow large armies of soldiers, battle tanks, aliens, and mechanized walkers to clash quickly and decisively. Players can field forces inspired by classic grim sci-fi tropes (power-armored warriors, alien hive creatures, etc.) with an emphasis on simplicity: all core rules fit on a couple of pages. Despite its brevity, Grimdark Future provides ample strategic depth through unit variety and customization, making for fast-playing battles that still require smart tactical choices.

name: Hail Caesar
description: A massed-battle historical miniatures game by Warlord Games, covering conflicts from antiquity through the Middle Ages . Players can refight battles from the Bronze Age up to around 1500 AD, commanding large 28 mm armies of ranked infantry, cavalry, and chariots. The rules are designed for grand scale engagements – units maneuver in formations and combat resolution is streamlined to handle dozens of units. Hail Caesar emphasizes fun and fluid play over hyper-detail, yet retains historical flavor, allowing Romans, Greeks, medieval knights, and more to be fielded and led to glory under an overall commander's strategy.

name: Infinity
description: A fast-paced science-fiction skirmish game by Corvus Belli set in a high-tech cyberpunk future . Players command small teams of elite operatives drawn from diverse futuristic factions, engaging in covert missions and firefights across dense urban battlefields. Infinity is known for its innovative ARO (Automatic Reaction Order) system that keeps both players active – even when it's not your turn, your troops can react by shooting or dodging . With an anime-inspired aesthetic, the game features highly detailed miniatures and emphasizes tactical movement, use of cover, hacking, and coordinated actions, resulting in cinematic, objective-driven battles."19 20 20 21 22 23 24 4 "Kings of War","WARGAME","A rank-and-file mass battle fantasy wargame by Mantic Games, known for its streamlined rules and big armies . Players lead regiments of classic fantasy troops (elves, dwarfs, orcs, undead, etc.) arranged on unit bases that move as cohesive blocks . The game is designed to be easy to learn and fast to play, minimizing bookkeeping (units either fight at full strength or are removed when defeated). Kings of War's clean mechanics and balanced army lists allow for large-scale battles resolved in a few hours, emphasizing maneuver, flank charges, and decisive clashes of colorful fantasy forces on the tabletop.

name: Konflikt '47
description: An alternate-history miniatures wargame set in a weird World War II where super-science and the occult collide . It builds on the Bolt Action rules, but introduces bizarre weaponry and units: lumbering mechs, undead infantry, genetically augmented soldiers, and other horror-tech fielded by the WWII factions. Players command forces of roughly platoon size (tanks, squads, and specialists), using the familiar order dice system to activate units. The game blends historical tactics with sci-fi elements – for example, U.S. walkers support infantry advances, or German Nachtjäger squads wield advanced Rift-tech. Konflikt '47 offers a pulpy twist on WWII strategy with dynamic and unpredictable gameplay .

name: Malifaux
description: A Gothic-steampunk horror skirmish game set in the otherworldly city of Malifaux. Players assemble crews of 5–10 unique characters led by a powerful Master, each drawn from factions like the Guild, Resurrectionists, or Neverborn . The game uses an innovative card-based “Fate Deck” instead of dice, so players flip cards to determine the outcome of duels and can cheat fate by strategically hand-managing cards . Objectives often involve schemes and tricks rather than straightforward elimination, encouraging clever play. With its rich narrative setting, Malifaux emphasizes character synergy and resource management, delivering a deep, story-driven skirmish experience of magic, monsters, and mayhem on the streets of a twisted Wild West.

name: Marvel: Crisis Protocol
description: A character-driven miniatures skirmish game set in the Marvel Universe . Players build a team of iconic superheroes or villains (such as Spider-Man, Iron Man, or Red Skull) and battle on a 3′×3′ city battlefield littered with terrain. The game features dynamic scenarios and allows characters to perform dramatic actions – throwing cars, using superpowers, or teaming up for combos. Each character has unique abilities represented on a stat card, and gameplay uses custom dice and a power meter resource system. Crisis Protocol captures the cinematic action of Marvel comics, as players maneuver their supers around buildings and objectives in fast, explosive battles.

name: Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game
description: A tabletop miniatures wargame set in the world of J.R.R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit . Players collect and paint forces of heroes, warriors, and creatures from Middle- earth, then use them to re-enact iconic battles or create their own scenarios. The game uses a model-by-model activation system: each figure moves and fights individually, allowing heroes like Aragorn or Legolas to perform epic feats on the battlefield. Emphasis is placed on thematic accuracy – stats and special rules closely reflect the films and books. From the skirmish at Weathertop to 25 25 26 26 27 27 28 29 5 the Battle of Pelennor Fields, this game lets players experience the thrill of Tolkien's battles through strategic maneuvering and heroic actions.

name: Mordheim
description: A classic skirmish game set in the Warhammer Fantasy world's doomed city of Mordheim. Players control small warbands (5–15 models) of scavengers – from human mercenaries and skaven to undead – searching the ruins for the precious Wyrdstone that fell from a comet . Mordheim features campaign play: warband members gain experience, suffer injuries, and acquire new gear between games, creating an evolving narrative. The gameplay emphasizes terrain- rich battlefields (the rubble-strewn city streets), with climbing, jumping, and hiding all integral. Scenarios include street fights, monster hunts, and treasure grabs, making each game a chaotic free-for-all of cutthroats in a dark, gothic setting poisoned by magic and greed.

name: Necromunda
description: A tabletop skirmish wargame of gang warfare set in the dystopian underhive of the Warhammer 40,000 universe . Players control rival gangs fighting for territory, wealth, and survival amid the cramped industrial sprawl of Necromunda's hive cities . Each gang is a handful of fighters equipped with makeshift weapons and cybernetic enhancements. The game uses an alternating activation system and involves detailed scenarios, from turf wars to ambushes. Necromunda's campaign system is a hallmark: gang members improve skills or suffer lasting injuries over time, and players manage their gang's income and equipment between battles. The result is a narrative-rich experience of underworld combat, where every skirmish can tilt the power balance in the hive.

name: Oathmark: Battles of the Lost Age
description: A mass-battle fantasy wargame (written by the creator of Frostgrave) that puts players in command of multiracial armies . Oathmark allows mixing humans, elves, dwarves, and orcs within one force, representing the kingdom you build. Armies maneuver in ranked units on the battlefield and engage in large-scale clashes using an intuitive ruleset that emphasizes command control and formation tactics. The game also features a kingdom-building campaign: victories can expand the realm, unlocking new unit types or improvements reflected in future battles. With classic fantasy troops and straightforward mechanics, Oathmark delivers the feel of old-school rank-and-flank warfare combined with a realm management aspect.

name: Pike & Shotte
description: A historical tabletop wargame from Warlord Games set in the 16th and 17th centuries, an era of pike blocks and early gunpowder warfare . The rules cover conflicts like the Thirty Years' War, English Civil Wars, and other Renaissance battles. Players command units of musketeers, pikemen, cavalry, and artillery in massed formations. Gameplay involves issuing orders to brigades and resolving combat with dice, with mechanics similar to Black Powder but tweaked for the distinctive tactics of the period (such as combined pike-and-shot infantry formations). Pike & Shotte emphasizes grand battles with colorful regimental units and encourages scenario play to reflect historical engagements of the early modern era.

name: Saga
description: A skirmish miniatures game set during the “heroic ages,” covering historical and mythological conflicts from the Dark Ages and beyond . Players take on the role of a warlord leading a small warband (~30 figures) of warriors, which could be Viking raiders, Crusaders, Samurai (in variant) or even fantastical creatures, depending on the setting. Saga's hallmark is its unique 30 31 31 32 33 34 6 Battle Board and Saga dice system: each faction has a board of abilities powered by special dice, allowing players to activate troops and trigger combat bonuses or tactics . This resource-management aspect adds depth to the simple core rules. The result is a game that rewards clever allocation of abilities and captures the flavor of each faction, whether it's shield-wall tactics for Anglo- Danes or berserker fury for Norsemen.

name: Spectre: Operations
description: A modern combat tabletop skirmish game focusing on special operations and realistic tactical action . Players command small teams of elite operatives or insurgents in scenarios inspired by 21st-century conflicts, from clandestine raids to urban firefights. The rules emphasize authenticity: line of sight, suppressive fire, and noise are important factors, and weapons have realistic ranges and effects. Stealth can be as viable as brute force – a player might attempt to complete objectives covertly before the alarm is raised. Spectre: Operations uses dice to resolve firefights and morale, delivering tense, fast lethal engagements that reward real-world tactics in a tabletop setting.

name: Star Wars: Armada
description: A tactical fleet miniatures game that puts players in control of the capital ships of the Star Wars universe . Players assume the role of fleet admirals, commanding Imperial Star Destroyers, Rebel cruisers, and support craft, while also coordinating starfighter squadrons. Gameplay involves plotting commands for ships (with a unique command dial system) and resolving combat with custom dice as massive vessels exchange turbolaser fire and launch fighters. Armada emphasizes careful maneuvering and timing – ships have momentum, and anticipating enemy movement is key. The scale and detail capture the feel of epic space engagements, from close-range broadside exchanges to fighter strikes against capital ships.

name: Star Wars: Legion
description: A two-player tactical miniatures game of ground battles in the Star Wars galaxy . Each player fields an army of iconic units from the Galactic Civil War era (Rebels vs Empire, or other factions in expansions) – squads of troopers, hero characters like Darth Vader or Luke Skywalker, as well as support vehicles (speeders, walkers). Legion uses an alternating activation system with command cards to influence turn order and special actions. Combat is resolved with custom dice, and terrain plays a crucial role as units take cover behind walls or in forests. The game's scenarios and objective-based play encourage thematic engagements where strategic use of characters' abilities can turn the tide of a battle.

name: Star Wars: X-Wing Miniatures Game
description: A fast-playing dogfight miniatures game set in the Star Wars universe . Players build squadrons of famous starfighters (X-wings, TIE fighters, etc.), each represented by a pre- painted miniature and pilot card, then engage in close-range space battles. X- Wing uses a maneuver dial system: players secretly choose maneuvers for each ship, then reveal and execute them, leading to tense prediction and bluffing gameplay. Firing is resolved with custom attack and defense dice. With its easy- to-learn rules and cinematic maneuvers, the game captures the feel of Star Wars dogfights – ships barrel-rolling, locking targets, and evading through asteroid fields in quick, tactical engagements.

name: Stargrave
description: A science-fiction skirmish wargame by Osprey Games that transposes Frostgrave's style of play to a ravaged galaxy . Players create a 35 36 37 38 39 40 7 crew of spacefaring adventurers led by a Captain (and second-in-command) from various backgrounds – ex-military, psionic, robotic, etc. These crews undertake missions on wartorn fringe worlds, seeking loot and information while facing off against rival crews and roaming threats. The game is miniatures-agnostic and campaign-driven: between scenarios, crew members can gain new gear and skills, and Captains improve their abilities. Stargrave's rules emphasize cover, ranged firefights, and sci-fi gadgets, providing a toolkit for cinematic skirmishes with lasers, hacking, and alien creatures, all while players try not to attract the attention of dominant pirate fleets or remnants of war.

name: Team Yankee
description: A fast-paced, tactical miniatures wargame set in an alternate Cold War gone hot in the 1980s . Based on the novel *Team Yankee*, the game portrays hypothetical battles between NATO and Warsaw Pact forces in Europe. Players command companies of modern armor and mechanized infantry – tanks like the M1 Abrams or T-72, IFVs, helicopters, and support units – in 15 mm scale. The rules emphasize realism and combined-arms tactics: line-of- sight, armor penetration, and unit morale are key factors . Scenarios often involve objectives like securing bridges or repelling breakthroughs. With its detailed yet playable system, Team Yankee delivers an immersive experience of high-intensity modern combat on the tabletop.

name: Test of Honour
description: A samurai-themed skirmish wargame played on a tabletop battlefield with roughly 5–20 models per side . Players build their force around a samurai hero and his retainers, which may include ashigaru spearmen, archers, and other warriors of feudal Japan . The game uses a draw bag activation system (with tokens determining whether a hero or common soldier acts) that creates uncertainty and tension each turn. Duels between samurai can be decisive, as special skills and combo attacks come into play. With quick, brutal combat and a focus on individual heroics and honor, Test of Honour evokes the feel of cinematic samurai encounters and clan battles in the Sengoku period.

name: The Ninth Age: Fantasy Battles
description: A community-created fantasy tabletop wargame that simulates mass battles between two high-fantasy armies with rank- and-file troops . It was developed as a spiritual successor to classic Warhammer Fantasy Battles. Players field regiments of miniature soldiers (on square bases) representing various fantasy races and creatures, maneuvering them in blocks across the battlefield . The Ninth Age features balanced, competitively tested rules and supports 16 factions, each with its own army book. Gameplay emphasizes tactical positioning, flanking, and resource management (magic dice and leadership) to rout the enemy's forces, all while maintaining a high degree of army customization and list-building depth.

name: Warhammer 40,000
description: A massive, futuristic war game set in the grim darkness of the 41st millennium, featuring countless factions waging endless war across the galaxy . Players collect and paint armies of miniature soldiers, aliens, and war machines (Space Marines, Orks, Tyranids, and many more), then engage in turn-based battles on the tabletop. The game uses a phase-based system (movement, psychic, shooting, charge, combat) and dice to resolve actions. Strategic unit positioning, combined-arms tactics, and list customization are key as players attempt to achieve objectives amid the carnage. Warhammer 40K's gameplay scales from small skirmishes to planet-shattering conflicts, allowing 41 41 42 43 44 45 46 8 everything from infantry firefights to titanic tank engagements in its rich, lore-heavy setting.

name: Warhammer 40,000: Kill Team
description: A fast-paced skirmish game set in the Warhammer 40K universe, focusing on small squads of elite operatives rather than large armies . Players assemble a Kill Team of typically 5–10 models (e.g. Space Marine infiltrators, Ork kommandos, Tau stealth suits) and battle opposing teams in tight, tactical missions. The game emphasizes individual model actions and uses an alternating activation system, creating tense back-and-forth play. Each operative has unique skills and equipment, and players can issue strategic ploys to gain an edge. With its compact 22″×30″ play area and dense terrain, Kill Team delivers an intense tactical experience where every decision, from positioning to target priority, can be decisive .

name: Warhammer Age of Sigmar
description: A fantasy miniatures wargame by Games Workshop set in the Mortal Realms – high-fantasy worlds of gods, monsters, and magic. Players command armies of miniatures representing grand alliances (Order, Chaos, Death, Destruction) clashing in epic battles. The game features streamlined rules and round bases, doing away with rank-and-file formations in favor of free-form unit movement. Phases cover movement, spellcasting, shooting, and melee, with distinctive command abilities for heroes. The setting's eight Realms allow for diverse forces (from Stormcast Eternals to Chaos Daemons) and fantastical battlegrounds. With its emphasis on heroes and big cinematic moments, Age of Sigmar offers mighty battles in an age of unending war .

name: Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Warcry
description: A skirmish combat game set in the Mortal Realms of Age of Sigmar, focusing on rival warbands fighting for glory in chaotic locales . Players control small warbands (typically ~8–15 models) – such as Chaos cultists, Ironjaw orruks, or Stormcast vanguards – and face off in fast, scenario-driven battles. Warcry's rules are very fast and action-oriented: units have a move and two actions each turn, and initiative is determined by dice rolls that can also unlock special “ability” moves . The game is played on a dense 22″×30″ battlefield with terrain like ruins or forests affecting movement and line of sight. Warcry emphasizes narrative play as well, with campaigns where warbands grow in power or suffer lasting injuries as they seek the favor of the gods.

name: Warhammer Fantasy Battles (6th Edition)
description: A classic rank-and-file fantasy wargame set in the Old World, featuring massed regiments of troops maneuvering in tight formations. Players lead armies of various races (Empire, Orcs, Skaven, etc.) and engage in large battles where units march in blocks, wheel to change facing, and charge home for bloody melees . The 6th Edition rules, in particular, brought a balanced and structured approach to gameplay, with clear turn sequences and emphasis on leadership and psychology (troop morale). Magic is present but risky, and characters (heroes and lords) bolster units rather than single-handedly winning battles. Overall, Warhammer Fantasy 6th delivers a strategic battlefield experience of maneuver warfare, flank attacks, and decisive cavalry charges in a rich, grim fantasy setting.

name: Warhammer Underworlds
description: A fast-paced game of tactical arena combat set in the Warhammer Age of Sigmar universe . It is a competitive miniatures board game hybrid where each player controls a small warband (3–7 fighters) locked in combat in a hex-grid arena. Warhammer Underworlds uniquely combines 47 48 48 49 50 50 51 52 9 deck-building with miniature combat: players build a deck of power and objective cards to support their warband and score points . Gameplay involves alternating activations, with fighters moving, attacking, or taking objectives, while players play cards for boosts or tricks. The matches are short (usually best-of-three format), and warbands are very thematic – from Stormcast Eternals to Skaven – each with a unique playstyle. Underworlds is often dubbed “the ultimate competitive miniatures game” for its tight rules and emphasis on skillful card and model play.

name: Warhammer: The Horus Heresy
description: A tabletop wargame set in the dark and tumultuous past of Warhammer 40K – the galaxy-spanning civil war known as the Horus Heresy . It focuses on battles between the Loyalist and Traitor Space Marine Legions, pitting superhuman warriors and colossal war machines against each other on a grand scale . The game uses rules similar to Warhammer 40,000's 7th edition, with an emphasis on Astartes armies and their Primarchs. Players can field large formations of Space Marines, tanks like Land Raiders and Spartans, and Knight or Titan support, reenacting legendary battles of the Heresy. Rich narrative elements and forge world models allow reenactment of specific crusade armies, making the Horus Heresy game a deeply immersive way to experience the iconic lore through tabletop conflict.

name: Warhammer: The Old World
description: Warhammer: The Old World is an epic, large-scale fantasy tabletop miniatures game produced by Games Workshop and rereleased in early 2024. It is a nostalgia project that revives and updates the rules and extensive lore of the classic Warhammer Fantasy Battles, which was discontinued in 2015. The game is set hundreds of years before the End Times, in the year 2276 IC, during a period known as The Age of Three Emperors. The Empire of Man is fragmented by civil wars, and the world faces threats from within and without, such as hordes of Beastmen, Orcs, Goblins, and the growing forces of Chaos in the north. Gameplay focuses on mass combat with units in ranked formations and flanks. Strategic positioning is crucial, as players must manoeuvre regiments of miniatures on square bases to outwit, outflank, and annihilate their opponent, utilizing a mix of infantry, cavalry, monsters, and war machines. It is a game with detailed rules and a six-sided dice system (2d6 for most rolls) that rewards tactical planning over simple individual combat.

name: Warmachine
description: Warmachine is a fast-paced, 35mm scale tabletop miniatures wargame set in the Iron Kingdoms, a steampunk-inspired world of tactical combat and mechanised warfare. The game, now owned and developed by Steamforged Games, pits players commanding powerful leaders known as warcasters against each other. Central to the gameplay are the mighty warjacks, large, steam-powered mechanical constructs armed with devastating weaponry that the warcasters control using a unique focus mechanic. The game uses a consistent 2d6 system for resolving actions and emphasizes strategic synergy and combos between different units. Victory is often achieved not just by destroying enemy troops, but by eliminating the opposing warcaster in a decisive assassination.
